title: SOHCAHTOA: read or build a trig ratio
subtitle: Right triangles and trigonometry · 17 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **17 of the official questions in Right triangles and trigonometry are this one** — 2 Easy, 5 Medium, 10 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You're asked for sin, cos, or tan of a marked angle in a right triangle whose sides are labeled, or you're given one trig ratio as a fraction and asked for a side length or a different ratio.
- The answer is often a fraction or a decimal you enter yourself.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) From the marked angle, label the sides opposite, adjacent, and hypotenuse.
- 2) If all the sides you need are shown, write the ratio (SOH-CAH-TOA).
- 3) If you're given a ratio, scale its sides by k, use Pythagoras to find the missing side, then use the actual length given to solve for k or to form the new ratio.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Useful for checking: set degree mode and type sin(angle) or cos(angle) when an angle is given.
It can't label opposite and adjacent for you, so it doesn't help when you only have side lengths, beyond simplifying the fraction.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You label opposite and adjacent from the wrong angle (usually the other acute angle), which gives you the complementary ratio.
When you're given a ratio, you treat its numbers as the actual side lengths instead of multiples of k.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
